vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: baoyu-post-to-weibo
Version: 1.60.0

The skill bundle provides tools to automate posting text, images, and Markdown articles to Weibo by controlling a Chrome instance via the DevTools Protocol (CDP). It utilizes platform-specific scripts (copy-to-clipboard.ts and paste-from-clipboard.ts) to simulate real system keystrokes and clipboard operations, which is a documented strategy to bypass anti-bot mechanisms. While the code uses high-risk system APIs like osascript, PowerShell, and process killing (weibo-utils.ts), these actions are transparently implemented and strictly necessary for the stated functionality. No evidence of data exfiltration, malicious persistence, or prompt-injection attacks was found.

llm.summary: The skill's files, runtime instructions, and required tools align with its stated purpose (automating posts to Weibo via a real Chrome instance), though it exercises intrusive browser- and OS-level actions that you should be aware of before enabling.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (post to Weibo) match the code and SKILL.md. The scripts automate Chrome via CDP, manipulate the clipboard, paste keystrokes, convert Markdown to HTML, and upload media — all expected for a tool that posts content and headline articles to Weibo.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions tell the agent to run local TypeScript scripts (via bun/npx) that interact with the user's Chrome profile, clipboard, and frontmost application. This is consistent with the feature set, but the SKILL.md explicitly says to kill existing Chrome CDP instances automatically on errors (pkill example) and to perform paste keystrokes. Those actions affect other user processes and the global clipboard and are intrusive; they are within the tool's remit but worth explicit consent.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No remote install or download step is declared; the skill ships scripts and a local vendor module. Required runtimes are bun or npx (reasonable for bundled TypeScript). No remote extract-from-URL install steps were found.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill does not declare required credentials and does not request unrelated secrets. It does read/resolve profile/config paths (home, XDG/AppData) and can reuse a Chrome profile; the SKILL.md and code reference an environment variable hint (WEIBO_BROWSER_CHROME_PATH) though it isn't declared in requires.env — this is reasonable but should be documented to avoid confusion. The skill will read local files (images, Markdown) and may download HTTPS images referenced in Markdown into a temp dir.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and no special privileges. The skill does not request permanent platform-wide presence or modify other skills. It reads/writes only its own temp files and profile directories as part of Chrome automation.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do exactly what it claims: open or launch Chrome with a profile, paste content, and upload media to Weibo. Before installing, note the following: (1) it will interact with your real Chrome profile (can reuse or create profile directories) — consider using a dedicated profile to avoid accidental cross-posting; (2) it performs clipboard copy and simulates real paste keystrokes (osascript/xdotool/powershell), and the SKILL.md instructs it to kill existing Chrome CDP instances automatically on errors (pkill examples) — these are intrusive OS-level actions, so ensure you are comfortable with them; (3) it can download HTTPS images referenced in Markdown into a temp directory; (4) there are no required API keys or secrets, but the code may read environment variables like WEIBO_BROWSER_CHROME_PATH if you set them — the skill does not declare that variable in metadata, so if you rely on that behavior set it intentionally. If you need stronger isolation, run the scripts in a controlled environment (dedicated user account, isolated Chrome profile, or VM) and review/approve any pkill-like behavior before allowing the agent to execute autonomously.
